s: Night is parent of the Furies (as mother)

s: the Furies possesses ancient rights (rights over vengeance and retribution)

s: Persuasion empowers Athena (to appease the Furies)

s: the Furies is honoured by Athens (as resident goddesses)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Furies has sanctuary the Furies' sanctuary (in the heart of Athens)

s: the Furies receives worship from Athena's citizens (through sacrifice and reverence)

s: the Furies controls mortals (through stern divine decrees)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Furies causes pestilence (when their vengeance is unleashed)
q: Shall scatter venom, to exude again In pestilence on men.

s: Palace of Atreus is a palace (at Mycenae)
q: _The Scene is the Palace of Atreus at Mycenae. In front of the Palace stand statues of the gods, and altars prepared for sacrifices._

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus serves Clytemnestra (in reverence of her authority)
q: O queen, I come in reverence of thy sway— For, while the ruler’s kingly seat is void, The loyal heart before his consort bends.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is a queen (of Argos and consort of the absent ruler)
q: But thou, O child of Tyndareus, Queen Clytemnestra, speak!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra rules Argos (while Agamemnon is absent)
q: For, while the ruler’s kingly seat is void, The loyal heart before his consort bends.

s: Clytemnestra leaves the altars
q: [_They turn to Clytemnestra, who leaves the altars and comes forward._

s: Clytemnestra knows destruction and enslavement of the city (through the beacon signal)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is a monarch (elder)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Mycenae contains Palace of Atreus
q: _The Scene is the Palace of Atreus at Mycenae. In front of the Palace stand statues of the gods, and altars prepared for sacrifices._

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Paris ravishes the wife

s: Paris ravishes Helen (from the home of the Atrides)

s: Helen is a wife (whose abduction causes the war)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Trojan War is fought for Helen (to recover her from Troy)
q: Her to buy back, in war and blood, Whom one did wed but many woo’d!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Greeks contains ships (a thousand vessels sent from Argos)
q: A thousand ships from Argive land Put forth to bear the martial band,

s: Greeks rights the kingdom’s wrong

s: destruction and enslavement of the city is reported by my lord

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Watchman keeps watch the watch (this livelong year)
q: I pray the gods to quit me of my toils, To close the watch I keep, this livelong year;

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: beacon-fire message travels through beacon fires (from mountain to mountain)
q: So sped from stage to stage, fulfilled in turn, Flame after flame, along the course ordained,

s: beacon fires are kindled by Hephaestus (as divine fire signals)
q: From Ida’s top Hephaestus, lord of fire, Sent forth his sign; and on, and ever on, Beacon to beacon sped the courier-flame.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: beacon fires connects Athos (from Ida)
q: From Ida to the crag, that Hermes loves, Of Lemnos; thence unto the steep sublime Of Athos, throne of Zeus, the broad blaze flared.

s: sacrifice of Agamemnon’s daughter is a sacrifice (performed to appease Artemis and enable the fleet to sail)
q: And so he steeled his heart—ah, well-a-day— Aiding a war for one false woman’s sake, His child to slay, And with her spilt blood make An offering, to speed the ships upon their way!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Iphigenia is a daughter (of Agamemnon)
q: Ill lot were mine, to disobey! And ill, to smite my child, my household’s love and pride! To stain with virgin blood a father’s hands, and slay My daughter, by the altar’s side!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Artemis opposes Agamemnon (because the eagles killed the unborn hare)
q: For virgin Artemis bears jealous hate Against the royal house, the eagle-pair, Who rend the unborn brood, insatiate— Yea, loathes their banquet on the quivering hare.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: omens at Aulis include eagles (a black eagle and a white-tailed eagle)
q: When on the right they soared across the sky, And one was black, one bore a white tail barred.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: omens at Aulis includes eagles (twy-coloured)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Calchas interprets omens at Aulis (as both favorable and dangerous)

s: omens at Aulis foretells Priam’s town (long the time shall be)

q: Zeus—if to The Unknown That name of many names seem good— Zeus, upon Thee I call.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Zeus teaches suffering as a source of wisdom (through affliction)
q: ’Tis Zeus alone who shows the perfect way Of knowledge: He hath ruled, Men shall learn wisdom, by affliction schooled.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: suffering as a source of wisdom comes from the gods (as a divine boon)
q: Comes wisdom o’er the unwilling soul— A boon, I wot, of all Divinity, That holds its sacred throne in strength, above the sky!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Fate takes Fate’s hard compelling yoke
q: Thus on his neck he took Fate’s hard compelling yoke;

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Trojan War returns warriors’ ashes (instead of the living men who departed)
q: For Ares, lord of strife, Who doth the swaying scales of battle hold, War’s money-changer, giving dust for gold, Sends back, to hearts that held them dear, Scant ash of warriors, wept with many a tear,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: ships depart from Greece (with the Greek army for Troy)
q: A thousand ships from Argive land Put forth to bear the martial band,

s: Watchman knows beacon-fire message (as the signal of Troy’s capture)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: ships commands the fleet of Greece
q: And then the elder chief, at whose command The fleet of Greece was manned,

s: ships are held by Artemis (through thwarting winds)
q: _Healer Apollo! be her wrath controll’d, Nor weave the long delay of thwarting gales, To war against the Danaans and withhold From the free ocean-waves their eager sails!_

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Argive host’s return is desired by Greeks (as a safe completion of the expedition)
q: For we need yet, before the race be won, Homewards, unharmed, to round the course once more.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Watchman wails the woe

s: Chorus is aged old (physically weakened and dependent on staffs)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus remains in home
q: And here at home we tarry, fain Our feeble footsteps to sustain, Each on his staff—so strength doth wane,

s: Rumour is roused by the joyful flame
q: Have the swift feet of Rumour hied, Roused by the joyful flame:

s: the news is uncertain truth or deception (until the herald speaks)
q: But is the news they scatter, sooth? Or haply do they give for truth Some cheat which heaven doth frame?

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Herald comes from the shore (wearing an olive-wreath)

s: destruction and enslavement of the city avoids a city to the dust

s: Troy's lords is buried in Troy (each in his Trojan grave)
q: And others, far beneath the Ilian wall, Sleep their last sleep—the goodly chiefs and tall, Couched in the foeman’s land, whereon they gave Their breath, and lords of Troy, each in his Trojan grave.

s: the city is heavy with suppressed wrath (because of the fallen)

s: the sons of carnage is subject to divine retribution (when the Furies come)
q: For not forgetful is the high gods’ doom Against the sons of carnage: all too long Seems the unjust to prosper and be strong, Till the dark Furies come, And smite with stern reversal all his home,

s: the Furies inflicts divine retribution (with stern reversal upon the guilty man's home)

s: divine retribution is sent by the gods (as a vengeful bolt)

s: Clytemnestra is a wife (of Agamemnon)

q: Trusty to keep for ten long years unmarred The store whereon he set his master-seal.

s: Herald returns to Argos (with news of victory)
q: O land of Argos, fatherland of mine! To thee at last, beneath the tenth year’s sun, My feet return

s: Menelaus is a lord of Argos (second well-loved)

s: Menelaus has unknown fate life or death
q: But say, what now of him each comrade saith? What their forebodings, of his life or death?

s: Helen is a bride (whose marriage brings war)
q: And named her, in her natal hour, Helen, the bride with war for dower?

s: Helen causes the Trojan War (through her departure from Sparta)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Paris is a robber (of Helen)
q: But at Fate’s judgment-seat the robber stands Condemned of rapine, and his prey is torn Forth from his hands

s: Paris causes Troy’s destruction (by taking Helen)
q: Woe upon Paris, woe and hate! Who wooed his country’s doom for mate

s: Zeus is a god (high-ruling and avenging)
q: and hail our country’s God, High-ruling Zeus

s: Zeus rights wrong

s: Apollo is a god (the Pythian lord)
q: and hail our country’s God, High-ruling Zeus, and thou, the Pythian lord

q: Whose arrows smote us once—smite thou no more! Was not thy wrath wreaked full upon our heads, O king Apollo, by Scamander’s side?

s: the gods judge Troy (in a heavenly council)

q: This sentence gave, _On Ilion and her men, Death:_

s: Greeks conquer Troy (in the Trojan War)

s: Agamemnon is a king (of Argos)

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Troy falls Ilion’s fall

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Troy is destroyed by the sack of Troy
q: Last night, when first the fiery courier came, In sign that Troy is ta’en and razed to earth

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Trojan War is fought for one woman’s sake

s: the sack of Troy destroys Troy (completely)
q: In sign that Troy is ta’en and razed to earth

s: Fate governs the Trojan War (as an appointed destiny)
q: Such mighty yoke of fate he set on Troy

q: What day beams fairer on a woman’s eyes Than this, whereon she flings the portal wide, To hail her lord, heaven-shielded, home from war?

s: Agamemnon praises Odysseus (as loyal and trustworthy)
q: One only—he who went reluctant forth Across the seas with me—Odysseus—he Was loyal unto me with strength and will, A trusty trace-horse bound unto my car.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is a wife (of Agamemnon)
q: First, that a wife sat sundered from her lord,

s: Agamemnon fights at Ilion (during its siege)

s: Agamemnon is a victor (returning from war)

s: Agamemnon is chief of Greeks (as its returning commander)
q: Gift of the army to its chief and lord.

s: Agamemnon possesses Agamemnon's car (on his return)
q: Sweet lord, step forth, Step from thy car, I pray

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon possesses Agamemnon's sandals (worn beneath his feet)
q: Then, if thou wilt, let some one stoop to loose Swiftly these sandals, slaves beneath my foot:

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus is a lieges (of Argos)
q: Old men of Argos, lieges of our realm,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus belongs to Argos (as subjects)
q: Old men of Argos, lieges of our realm,

s: Orestes is a child (of Clytemnestra and Agamemnon)
q: Hence haps it that Orestes, thine and mine,

s: Orestes is guarded by Strophius (loyally in Phocis)
q: he dwells with one Who guards him loyally; ’tis Phocis’ king, Strophius

s: Troy is a city (besieged by Agamemnon)
q: The while my lord beleaguered Ilion’s wall.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Ilion is a city (whose wall Agamemnon besieged)
q: The while my lord beleaguered Ilion’s wall.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Trojan War takes place at Troy
q: Thy lord in daily jeopardy at Troy,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon's return is a homecoming (to his hearth and home)
q: And thou, returning to thine hearth and home,

s: Agamemnon's return brings joy (to the household)
q: Such boons and more doth bring into a home The present footstep of its proper lord.

q: Women! why tarry ye, whose task it is To spread your monarch’s path with tapestry?

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: purple robes contains purple dye (as their coloring substance)
q: A Sea there is—and who shall stay its springs? And deep within its breast, a mighty store, Precious as silver, of the purple dye, Whereby the dipped robe doth its tint renew.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is married to Agamemnon
q: The pledge and symbol of our wedded troth,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: purple robes is a costly garments (worth silver-like wealth)
q: Precious as silver, of the purple dye, Whereby the dipped robe doth its tint renew.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is a slave (captured in war)
q: None willingly Wear the slave’s yoke—and she, the prize and flower Of all we won, comes hither in my train

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra belongs to Greeks (as a prize of war given to its chief)
q: Gift of the army to its chief and lord.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Greeks gives a gift (to its chief and lord)
q: Gift of the army to its chief and lord.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the gods is a divine beings (distinguished from mortals)
q: such pomp beseems the gods, Not me. A mortal man

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Zeus is a god (lord of fulfilment)
q: Zeus, Zeus, Fulfilment’s lord! my vows fulfil

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Rumour bodes evil (rumour’s many tongues)
q: And woe, to hear how rumour’s many tongues All boded evil—woe, when he who came And he who followed spake of ill on ill, Keening _Lost, lost, all lost!_ thro’ hall and bower.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is parent of Orestes (mother)
q: Hence haps it that Orestes, thine and mine,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra rules Argos (as queen)
q: Old men of Argos, lieges of our realm,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is a king
q: Step from thy car, I pray—nay, not on earth Plant the proud foot, O king, that trod down Troy!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is married to Clytemnestra (husband)
q: So sweet it is to ’scape the press of pain. With such salute I bid my husband hail!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is a mortal man
q: Not unto me, as to some Eastern lord, Bowing thyself to earth, make homage loud. Strew not this purple that shall make each step An arrogance; such pomp beseems the gods, Not me. A mortal man to set his foot On these rich dyes?

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon fights at Troy (during the siege)
q: The while my lord beleaguered Ilion’s wall.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is a prophetess (of Troy)
q: Yea—prophetess to Troy of all her doom.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus is a collective of Argives (loyal to Agamemnon)
q: ’Tis best, I judge, aloud for aid to call, “Ho! loyal Argives! to the palace, all!”

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus fears the murder of Agamemnon (after hearing his cries)
q: The bloody act is over—I have heard the monarch’s cry— Let us swiftly take some counsel, lest we too be doomed to die.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus recognizes Cassandra (as prophetic)
q: She grows presageful of her woes to come, Slave tho’ she be, instinct with prophecy.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is a wedded wife (of Agamemnon)
q: A wedded wife, she slays her lord, Helped by another hand!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is a murderer (of Agamemnon)
q: O aweless soul! the woman slays her lord—

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra plots the murder of Agamemnon (with an accomplice)
q: A wedded wife, she slays her lord, Helped by another hand!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is compared to a lioness (couching while her mate is away)
q: Lo, how the woman-thing, the lioness Couched with the wolf—her noble mate afar— Will slay me, slave forlorn!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon suffers a deep, a mortal blow
q: VOICE OF AGAMEMNON O I am sped—a deep, a mortal blow.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is a lord of ships (victor at Troy)
q: And he, the lord of ships, who trod down Troy,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is a slave (within the house of Atreus)
q: Slave tho’ she be, instinct with prophecy.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is unaware of the fawning treachery of tongue
q: My master—mine—I bear the slave’s yoke now, And he, the lord of ships, who trod down Troy, Knows not the fawning treachery of tongue Of this thing false and dog-like

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is killed in the murder of Agamemnon (inside the palace)
q: VOICE OF AGAMEMNON O! O! again, another, another blow!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Apollo is a god (of prophecy and ways)
q: Apollo, Apollo! God of all ways, but only Death’s to me,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Apollo grants the prophetic gift (to Cassandra)
q: That is my power—a boon Apollo gave.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Apollo revokes the prophetic gift (after Cassandra rejects him)
q: Look! it is he, it is Apollo’s self Rending from me the prophet-robe he gave.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Zeus wills Asclepius (to die as a warning)
q: So Zeus hath willed: Else had he spared the leech Asclepius, skilled To bring man from the dead: the hand divine Did smite himself with death—a warning and a sign.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Furies inhabit the house of Atreus (as avenging spirits)
q: Within this house a choir abidingly Chants in harsh unison the chant of ill; Yea, and they drink, for more enhardened joy, Man’s blood for wine, and revel in the halls, Departing never, Furies of the home.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Furies drink human blood (for revelry)
q: Yea, and they drink, for more enhardened joy, Man’s blood for wine, and revel in the halls,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the house of Atreus is cursed the curse of the house of Atreus (by ancestral crimes)
q: Home cursed of God! Bear witness unto me, Ye visioned woes within— The blood-stained hands of them that smite their kin

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Troy falls Ilion
q: Woe for my city, woe for Ilion’s fall!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is born beyond the seas
q: Yet how should oath—how loyally soe’er I swear it—aught avail thee? In good sooth, My wonder meets thy claim: I stand amazed That thou, a maiden born beyond the seas, Dost as a native know and tell aright Tales of a city of an alien tongue.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Troy is destroyed in destruction and enslavement of the city (after its towers are shattered)
q: Low lie the shattered towers whereas they fell,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Palace of Atreus contains a choir (within this house)
q: Within this house a choir abidingly Chants in harsh unison the chant of ill;

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the prophetic gift is granted by Apollo (to Cassandra)
q: That is my power—a boon Apollo gave.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the curse of the house of Atreus is caused by Thyestes’ feast (among other ancestral crimes)
q: Ah—’tis Thyestes’ feast on kindred flesh— I guess her meaning and with horror thrill,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the murder of Agamemnon is committed by Clytemnestra (with another hand assisting)
q: A wedded wife, she slays her lord, Helped by another hand!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra’s death is a sacrifice (a bloody slaughter in the palace)
q: But me a slaughter-house and block of blood Shall see hewn down, a reeking sacrifice.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Thyestes’ feast is a crime (involving kindred flesh)
q: Ah—’tis Thyestes’ feast on kindred flesh—

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the vengeance for Agamemnon’s murder is carried out by Orestes (to avenge his father’s blood)
q: He, to avenge his father’s blood outpoured, Shall smite and slay with matricidal hand.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra possesses the prophetic gift (granted by Apollo)
q: That is my power—a boon Apollo gave.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is loved by Apollo (formerly)
q: Once and again, O thou, Destroyer named, Thou hast destroyed me, thou, my love of old!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra foils Apollo (after pledging herself to him)
q: Nay—for I plighted troth, then foiled the god.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra foresees the murder of Agamemnon (through prophecy)
q: ’Tis Agamemnon’s doom thou shalt behold.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra foresees Cassandra’s death (as an imminent sacrifice)
q: Yet shall the gods have heed of me who die, For by their will shall one requite my doom.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is destined for Cassandra’s death (inside the palace)
q: But me a slaughter-house and block of blood Shall see hewn down, a reeking sacrifice.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is the father of Iphigenia (sacrificed daughter)
q: His daughter, blossom of my womb, He gave unto a deadly doom, Iphigenia, child of tears!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is killed in the killing of Orestes's father (by Clytemnestra)
q: Lo! at my feet lies Agamemnon slain, My husband once—and him this hand of mine, A right contriver, fashioned for his death.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon be dead lord of all
q: And now lies dead the lord of all.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon takes Cassandra (as captive prize and paramour)
q: Behold him dead—behold his captive prize, Seeress and harlot—comfort of his bed, True prophetess, true paramour

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is a seeress (captive of Agamemnon)
q: Behold him dead—behold his captive prize, Seeress and harlot—comfort of his bed, True prophetess, true paramour

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is a captive (war captive and prize of Agamemnon)
q: Behold him dead—behold his captive prize, Seeress and harlot—comfort of his bed,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Cassandra is killed with Agamemnon (laid beside him after death)
q: The body of Agamemnon lies, muffled in a long robe, within a silver-sided laver; the corpse of Cassandra is laid beside him.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Aegisthus is the lover of Clytemnestra (current partner)
q: While in this hearth and home of mine there burns The light of love—Aegisthus—as of old Loyal, a stalwart shield of confidence

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Aegisthus is the son of Thyestes (youngest child)
q: For me, an infant yet in swaddling bands, Of the three children youngest, Atreus sent To banishment by my sad father’s side

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Aegisthus plans the killing of Orestes's father (with Clytemnestra)
q: And I—who else?—this murder wove and planned;

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is the wife of Agamemnon (slain husband)
q: Lo! at my feet lies Agamemnon slain, My husband once—and him this hand of mine, A right contriver, fashioned for his death.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Aegisthus rule the palace (with Clytemnestra)
q: I and thou will rule the palace and will order all things well.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Aegisthus is a ruler (of Argos)
q: Ruler? but ’tis not for Argives, thus to own a dastard lord!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes return homeward way (if Fortune guide him safely)
q: Not if Fortune guide Orestes safely on his homeward way.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Iphigenia is the daughter of Clytemnestra (murdered child)
q: Yea, slew in sacrifice his child and mine, The well-loved issue of my travail-pangs,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Iphigenia is the daughter of Agamemnon (sacrificed daughter)
q: His daughter, blossom of my womb, He gave unto a deadly doom, Iphigenia, child of tears!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Iphigenia be given a deadly doom (by Agamemnon)
q: His daughter, blossom of my womb, He gave unto a deadly doom, Iphigenia, child of tears!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Atreus is the father of Agamemnon (father of the slain king)
q: Take ye the truth, that Atreus, this man’s sire, The lord and monarch of this land of old,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Atreus perpetrates Thyestes’ feast (against Thyestes)
q: But Atreus, godless sire Of him who here lies dead, this welcome planned— With zeal that was not love he feigned to hold In loyal joy a day of festal cheer, And bade my father to his board, and set Before him flesh that was his children once.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Thyestes is the brother of Atreus (rival brother)
q: Brother with brother, for the prize of sway, And drave him from his home to banishment.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is the mother of Iphigenia (murdered daughter)
q: Yea, slew in sacrifice his child and mine, The well-loved issue of my travail-pangs,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Helen causes Trojan War (through her infatuation)
q: O Helen, O infatuate soul, Who bad’st the tides of battle roll, O’erwhelming thousands, life on life, ’Neath Ilion’s wall!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Zeus is a god (high cause and finisher of all)
q: Ah woe, ah Zeus! from Zeus all things befall— Zeus the high cause and finisher of all!— Lord of our mortal state, by him are willed All things, by him fulfilled!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Furies strike the lord of Atreus’ house (for Atreus and his feast of blood)
q: The old Avenger, stern of mood For Atreus and his feast of blood, Hath struck the lord of Atreus’ house

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Fate governs the house of Atreus (through inherited doom)
q: The children of the curse abide within These halls of high estate— And none can wrench from off the home of sin The clinging grasp of fate.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Justice take him (in Justice’ ambush)
q: And death itself were honour now to me, Beholding him in Justice’ ambush ta’en.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus is a elders (of Argos)
q: Elders of Argos—since the thing stands so,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Chorus opposes Aegisthus (politically and morally)
q: Aegisthus, for this insolence of thine That vaunts itself in evil, take my scorn.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the house of Atreus contains blood vengeance (inherited disposition)
q: Right was that word—thou namest well The brooding race-fiend, triply fell! From him it is that murder’s thirst, Blood-lapping, inwardly is nursed— Ere time the ancient scar can sain, New blood comes welling forth again.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Argos is ruled by Clytemnestra (with Aegisthus)
q: I and thou will rule the palace and will order all things well.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is the lover of Aegisthus (current partner and political ally)
q: While in this hearth and home of mine there burns The light of love—Aegisthus—as of old Loyal, a stalwart shield of confidence

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the killing of Orestes's father be committed by my right hand
q: And I—who else?—this murder wove and planned; For me, an infant yet in swaddling bands, Of the three children youngest, Atreus sent To banishment by my sad father’s side: But Justice brought me home once more, grown now To manhood’s years; and stranger tho’ I was, My right hand reached unto the chieftain’s life, Plotting and planning all that malice bade.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Thyestes’ feast is perpetrated by Atreus (against Thyestes)
q: But Atreus, godless sire Of him who here lies dead, this welcome planned— With zeal that was not love he feigned to hold In loyal joy a day of festal cheer, And bade my father to his board, and set Before him flesh that was his children once.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: blood vengeance be nursed murder’s thirst (inwardly)
q: From him it is that murder’s thirst, Blood-lapping, inwardly is nursed— Ere time the ancient scar can sain, New blood comes welling forth again.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra kill Agamemnon
q: Lo! at my feet lies Agamemnon slain, My husband once—and him this hand of mine, A right contriver, fashioned for his death.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra rules Argos (with Aegisthus)
q: I and thou will rule the palace and will order all things well.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is an instrument of the Furies (as avenger of the house)
q: The old Avenger, stern of mood For Atreus and his feast of blood, Hath struck the lord of Atreus’ house, And in the semblance of his wife The king hath slain

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon be a king
q: Yet ah my king, my king no more! What words to say, what tears to pour Can tell my love for thee?

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is the husband of Clytemnestra (slain husband)
q: Lo! at my feet lies Agamemnon slain, My husband once—and him this hand of mine, A right contriver, fashioned for his death.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes be a son my father
q: For O my father, not beside thy corse Stood I to wail thy death, nor was my hand Stretched out to bear thee forth to burial.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Chorus is a captive women (enslaved attendants from Troy)
q: And upon me—ah me!—the gods have laid The woe that wrapped round Troy, What time they led down from home and kin Unto a slave’s employ

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Chorus serves the palace household (as enslaved palace attendants)
q: Hand maidens, orderers of the palace-halls, Since at my side ye come, a suppliant train,

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Chorus bears libations (by royal command for Agamemnon’s grave)
q: Forth from the royal halls by high command I bear libations for the dead.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon be murdered majesty (at home)
q: O hearth of woe and bane, O state that low doth lie! Sunless, accursed of men, the shadows brood Above the home of murdered majesty.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon has Tomb of Agamemnon (as his grave-mound)
q: On this my country; lo, my foot is set On this grave-mound

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is a mother (of Orestes and Electra)
q: Homeless we are and sold; and she who sold Is she who bore us;

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Aegisthus be a lord her new lord
q: Aegisthus, her new lord.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Tomb of Agamemnon is in Mycenae (at the royal grave-mound)
q: _The Scene is the Tomb of Agamemnon at Mycenae; afterwards, the Palace of Atreus, hard by the Tomb._

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: libations be for the dead
q: Forth from the royal halls by high command I bear libations for the dead.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the gods are called on to av enge the murder of Agamemnon (through Orestes and divine justice)
q: Grant, O Zeus, Grant me my father’s murder to avenge— Be thou my willing champion!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Earth be a mother my nursing mother
q: O Earth, my nursing mother!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: blood guilt cannot be cleansed blood (after murder)
q: Lo, when man’s force doth ope The virgin doors, there is nor cure nor hope For what is lost,—even so, I deem, Though in one channel ran Earth’s every stream, Laving the hand defiled from murder’s stain, It were vain.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: mourning is expressed by the Chorus (through lamentation and bodily self-wounding)
q: Rings on my smitten breast my smiting hand, And all my cheek is rent and red, Fresh-furrowed by my nails, and all my soul This many a day doth feed on cries of dole.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes is in Orestes’ exile (as a banished returnee)
q: Me who from banishment returning stand On this my country; lo, my foot is set

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes discern these women (in suppliance)
q: Pass we aside, till rightly I discern Wherefore these women throng in suppliance.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes possesses the lock of hair (shorn as offerings and mourning tokens)
q: And these twin locks, from mine head shorn, I bring, And one to Inachus the river-god, My young life’s nurturer, I dedicate, And one in sign of mourning unfulfilled I lay, though late, on this my father’s grave.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Electra be a daughter my father
q: Father, my prayer is said; ’tis thine to hear— Grant that some fair fate bring Orestes home, And unto me grant these—a purer soul Than is my mother’s, a more stainless hand.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Electra be a child my father
q: And lo! in truth the hair exceeding like— CHORUS Like to what locks and whose? instruct me that. ELECTRA Like unto those my father’s children wear.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Electra offers libations (at Agamemnon’s grave)
q: Thus have I prayed, and thus I shed these streams, And follow ye the wont, and as with flowers Crown ye with many a tear and cry the dirge, Your lips ring out above the dead man’s grave. [_She pours the libations_

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Electra has Electra’s prayer (for Orestes’ return and vengeance on the slayers)
q: Father, my prayer is said; ’tis thine to hear— Grant that some fair fate bring Orestes home, And unto me grant these—a purer soul Than is my mother’s, a more stainless hand._ These be my prayers for us; for thee, O sire, I cry that one may come to smite thy foes, And that the slayers may in turn be slain

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes is a son of Agamemnon
q: O father, murdered in unkingly wise, Fulfil my prayer, grant me thine halls to sway.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Electra is a sister of Orestes (his only surviving close support)
q: And for myself I love thee—thee that wast A brother leal, sole stay of love to me.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Electra is a orphaned child (homeless)
q: Lo! I and she, Electra, stand before thee, fatherless, And each alike cast out and homeless made.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Electra seek dark death (unto Aegisthus)
q: To me too, grant this boon—dark death to deal Unto Aegisthus, and to ’scape my doom.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon be a father my father
q: O father, murdered in unkingly wise, Fulfil my prayer, grant me thine halls to sway.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is a father of Orestes and Electra
q: Lo! at thy tomb, two fledglings of thy brood— A man-child and a maid; hold them in ruth, Nor wipe them out, the last of Pelops’ line.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon be murdered father
q: Nay O father, I were fain Other fate had fallen on thee. Ill it were if thou hadst lain One among the common slain, Fallen by Scamander’s side— Those who slew thee there should be!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Agamemnon is honoured at Tomb of Agamemnon (by Orestes and Electra)
q: O father, to thy loved ones come in aid. ELECTRA With tears I call on thee

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra is a murderer of Agamemnon (acting with dishonour)
q: Aweless in hate, O mother, sternly brave! As in a foeman’s grave Thou laid’st in earth a king, but to the bier No citizen drew near,— Thy husband, thine, yet for his obsequies, Thou bad’st no wail arise

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra bear the serpent (from her womb)
q: Yea, from herself; her womb a serpent bare.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes is a brother of Electra
q: I, I am he; seek not one more akin.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Aegisthus is a slayer of Agamemnon (with Clytemnestra)
q: Unless upon the slayers of my sire I pressed for vengeance: this the god’s command

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Zeus is a parent of Orestes and Electra (their sole divine parent)
q: Zeus, thou alone to us art parent now.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Zeus is invoked by Orestes (for aid and justice)
q: Zeus, Zeus! look down on our estate and us, The orphaned brood of him, our eagle-sire, Whom to his death a fearful serpent brought

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Apollo is a god and prophet (authoritative and undisproved)
q: Apollo, king and prophet undisproved

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Apollo commands the vengeance for Agamemnon’s murder (through his oracle)
q: Unless upon the slayers of my sire I pressed for vengeance: this the god’s command

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Furies are a avenging powers (of the slain)
q: Where, where are ye, avenging powers, Puissant Furies of the slain?

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Furies pursue Orestes (for Agamemnon’s blood)
q: He spake moreover of assailing fiends Empowered to quit on me my father’s blood, Wreaking their wrath on me

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the Chorus be a the loyal band
q: Swiftly this cry arises—even so Pray we, the loyal band, as we have prayed!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes be fatherless fatherless
q: Lo! I and she, Electra, stand before thee, fatherless, And each alike cast out and homeless made.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the house of Atreus is a kingly stock (threatened with extinction)
q: So, if this kingly stock be withered all, None on high festivals will fend thy shrine

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the house of Atreus is afflicted by the curse of the house of Atreus (inherited and bloodstained)
q: Alas, the inborn curse that haunts our home, Of Atè’s bloodstained scourge the tuneless sound!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Tomb of Agamemnon is a sepulchre of Agamemnon (site of invocation)
q: Hear me too, even me, O father, hear! Not by one child alone these groans, these tears are shed Upon thy sepulchre.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Palace of Atreus be a seat of my father (where once my father sat)
q: and if I cross The threshold of the gate, the palace’ guard, And find him throned where once my father sat

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra’s dream contains the serpent (born from Clytemnestra’s womb)
q: Yea, from herself; her womb a serpent bare.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Clytemnestra’s dream slay her (in semblance of a serpent)
q: The rede is clear: the thing of dread she nursed, The death of blood she dies; and I, ’tis I, In semblance of a serpent, that must slay her.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the serpent is a child of Clytemnestra (in the dream)
q: for mark, that serpent sprang From the same womb as I, in swaddling bands By the same hands was swathed, lipped the same breast

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the serpent represents Orestes (in Clytemnestra’s dream)
q: and I, ’tis I, In semblance of a serpent, that must slay her.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the offerings send these offerings
q: She sends these offerings, in hope to win A cure to cleave and sunder sin from doom.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the lock of hair be shorn for my father’s grave
q: My very face thou see’st and know’st me not, And yet but now, when thou didst see the lock Shorn for my father’s grave

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the vengeance for Agamemnon’s murder is a command of Apollo (to be carried out by Orestes)
q: Unless upon the slayers of my sire I pressed for vengeance: this the god’s command

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the killing of Orestes's father call for other bloodshed (calling guilt of olden time)
q: Blood-drops shed upon the ground Plead for other bloodshed yet; Loud the call of death doth sound, Calling guilt of olden time

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the planned murder of Clytemnestra and Aegisthus slay the slayers (with a craft like theirs)
q: That I, in ire for home and wealth despoiled, Should with a craft like theirs the slayers slay

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Justice is a avenger of unlawful deeds (working in appointed time)
q: But Justice hath planted the anvil, and Destiny forgeth the sword That shall smite in her chosen time; by her is the child restored

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: the curse of the house of Atreus is a inborn curse (bloodstained and persistent)
q: Alas, the inborn curse that haunts our home, Of Atè’s bloodstained scourge the tuneless sound!

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes seeks the vengeance for Agamemnon’s murder (as a sacred obligation)
q: Unless upon the slayers of my sire I pressed for vengeance: this the god’s command

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes come to the palace gates (in likeness of a stranger)
q: I with this warrior Pylades will come In likeness of a stranger, full equipt As travellers come, and at the palace gates Will stand, as stranger yet in friendship’s bond Unto this house allied; and each of us Will speak the tongue that round Parnassus sounds, Feigning such speech as Phocian voices use.

l: The House of Atreus; Being the Agamemnon, the Libation-Bearers, and the Furies
s: Orestes is assisted by Pylades (in the planned vengeance)
q: I with this warrior Pylades will come
